findings.evidence: `head -8 TauCeti/AlgebraicTopology/UniversalCover/Action.lean` → `Copyright (c) 2026 Lean FRO, LLC. All rights reserved.` / `Authors: Kim Morrison`; `grep -rh 'Copyright (c)' TauCeti --include='*.lean' | sort | uniq -c` → 32+31 files under `Chris Birkbeck`, 7 under `Lean FRO, LLC`, 1 `Joseph Tooby-Smith`. `grep -rn -i 'vendor|adapted from' AGENTS.md` returns nothing, so this paragraph is the sole header rule agents will read.
findings.fix: Add a carve-out sentence: when a file is vendored from or closely adapted from Mathlib or another project, preserve the source file's copyright line and `Authors:` line verbatim rather than copying a neighbouring Tau Ceti block; the neighbouring-file rule applies only to originally-authored files.
findings.issue: The instruction to copy the neighbouring `Copyright (c) <year> The Tau Ceti contributors` block is unconditional, and the `Authors:` sentence is framed around whether the new file has named human authors rather than whether its source does. Applied to a file vendored or closely adapted from Mathlib or another Lean project, it directs an agent to replace the upstream copyright holder and authors with the Tau Ceti block — exactly the laundering the attribution rubric forbids. The repo already practices the opposite: `TauCeti/AlgebraicTopology/UniversalCover/Action.lean` carries `Copyright (c) 2026 Lean FRO, LLC` / `Authors: Kim Morrison`, and 63 files carry `Copyright (c) 20xx Chris Birkbeck`.

summary: The note is factually accurate about the lakefile and the header state, and needs no source credit of its own. But it is now the only place AGENTS.md states the header rule, and its unconditional "copy the copyright block from a neighbouring file" instruction contradicts the credit-carrying headers already in the tree for vendored/adapted material.
